The company is set to release a new product. → Компания, как ожидается/планирует, выпустит новый продукт.
The system is on the verge of crashing. → Система на грани сбоя.
Prices are likely to rise. → Вероятно, цены вырастут.
Special cases / exceptions: About to = very near future. Не все future expressions interchangeable.
Common mistakes: ❌ The train is about to arrive at six. (может звучать как «вот-вот», не timetable) → Для timetable better: due to arrive.
Don't confuse with: Сначала определи: schedule, immediate future, planned/expected event or probability.
Quick summary / memory hook:
due to = scheduled.
about to = very soon.
set to = expected/planned.
on the verge of = almost happening.
likely/expected to = probability/expectation.

Core idea: Future in the past описывает то, что было будущим относительно некоторого момента в прошлом.
Main rule / explanation: Was/were going to = past intention. Would = future from past viewpoint. Was/were about to = immediate future from past viewpoint. Was/were due to = scheduled future from past viewpoint.
Form / structure: was/were going to + V1. would + V1. was/were about to + V1. was/were due to + V1.
When / why we use it: Главное — past viewpoint: At 9 a.m. I knew that I would finish by noon.
Examples:
I was going to call you, but I forgot. → Я собирался тебе позвонить, но забыл.
He said he would help. → Он сказал, что поможет.
We were about to leave when she arrived. → Мы уже собирались уходить, когда она пришла.
The train was due to arrive at noon. → Поезд должен был прибыть в полдень.
Special cases / exceptions: Would here is not conditional; it means future relative to past. Do not switch automatically to will after a past reporting verb.
Common mistakes: ❌ He said he will help. → ✅ He said he would help.
Don't confuse with: Compare viewpoint now vs then: I will finish. / I knew I would finish.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Future from past viewpoint:
was going to.
would.
was about to.
was due to.

Lesson / Topic: Ellipsis and substitution – Omitting or replacing words
Core idea: Ellipsis — пропуск слов, которые легко восстановить из контекста. Substitution — замена повторяющейся структуры другим словом/выражением.
Main rule / explanation: Ellipsis removes understood material. Substitution uses words such as one, ones, do, so, neither to avoid repetition.
Form / structure: want to / promise to / me to etc. can leave understood words. so/neither/do/one/ones replace repeated material.
When / why we use it: Используем, чтобы речь звучала естественнее и не повторяла уже понятное.
Examples:
I can help if you want me to. → Я могу помочь, если хочешь, чтобы я помог.
She didn't call, although she promised to. → Она не позвонила, хотя обещала.
I need a new laptop. So does Anna. → Мне нужен новый ноутбук. Анне тоже.
I don't like the first option, but I like the second one. → Мне не нравится первый вариант, но второй нравится.
Special cases / exceptions: Ellipsis works only when missing information is recoverable from context. Не удаляй слова, если получится ambiguity.
Common mistakes:
❌ I chose the blue report because the blue report was clearer. → ✅ I chose the blue report because it was clearer.
❌ Убирать слова, которые нельзя восстановить по контексту. → ✅ Пропускай только то, что собеседник легко понимает.
Don't confuse with: Спроси: может ли listener восстановить missing words without guessing?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Ellipsis = omit understood words.
Substitution = replace repeated material.
Context must make meaning clear.

Core idea: English может объединять nouns в compound nouns и использовать possessive 's для ownership, relationship и некоторых time expressions.
Main rule / explanation: Compound noun: software developer, data analysis, customer service. Possessive 's: singular owner, plural possessive with apostrophe, irregular plural with 's.
Form / structure: noun + noun. singular noun + 's + noun. plural ending -s + apostrophe. irregular plural + 's.
When / why we use it: Определи, описывает ли первый noun type/purpose второго или показывает принадлежность/relationship.
Examples:
software developer → разработчик ПО.
data analysis → анализ данных.
the manager's office → офис менеджера.
the employees' room → комната сотрудников.
the children's books → детские книги.
today's meeting → сегодняшняя встреча.
two weeks' holiday → двухнедельный отпуск.
Special cases / exceptions: Plural noun ending in -s takes only apostrophe: students'. Irregular plural takes 's: children's.
Common mistakes:
❌ the students's projects → ✅ the students' projects.
❌ the children books → ✅ the children's books.
Don't confuse with: Compound noun = type/purpose. Possessive = relationship/ownership/time expression.
Quick summary / memory hook:
noun+noun = compound noun.
's = singular/irregular possessive.
s' = regular plural possessive.

Core idea: Cleft sentences делят информацию на части, чтобы один элемент получил особое emphasis.
Main rule / explanation: It-cleft: It was + focus + who/that... Wh-cleft: What + clause + be + focus. Можно выделить person, thing, time, place, reason.
Form / structure: It was X who/that + clause. What + clause + is/was + focus.
When / why we use it: Используем, когда важно исправить, уточнить или специально подчеркнуть элемент.
Examples:
It was John who called me. → Это Джон мне позвонил.
It was the deadline that caused the problem. → Именно deadline вызвал проблему.
What I need is more time. → Что мне нужно — это больше времени.
What she wanted was a clear answer. → Чего она хотела — это ясного ответа.
Special cases / exceptions: Cleft нужен, когда мы специально выделяем часть информации: человека, предмет, место, время или причину.
Common mistakes:
❌ It was John who called me yesterday. (если нет причины делать акцент) → ✅ John called me yesterday.
❌ What I need is more time? → ✅ What I need is more time. (это cleft-структура, а не вопрос.)
Don't confuse with: Спроси: какой элемент я хочу выделить? Если ни один — обычное предложение может быть лучше.
Quick summary / memory hook:
It-cleft = It was X who/that...
Wh-cleft = What ... is/was X.
Главная функция = emphasis.

Core idea: Relative clauses уточняют noun. Defining identifies exactly which person/thing; non-defining adds extra information and uses commas.
Main rule / explanation: Defining can use who/which/that/where/whose. Non-defining uses who/which/whose, not standard that. Object relative pronoun can sometimes be omitted.
Form / structure: Defining: noun + who/which/that + clause. Non-defining: noun, who/which/whose + clause,.
When / why we use it: Используем defining/non-defining relative clauses, чтобы идентифицировать noun или добавить дополнительную информацию.
Examples:
The report that you sent is useful. → Отчёт, который ты отправил, полезен.
The report, which you sent yesterday, is useful. → Отчёт, который ты отправил вчера, полезен.
The office where I work is nearby. → Офис, где я работаю, рядом.
The report (that) I sent was approved. → Отчёт, который я отправил, был одобрен.
Special cases / exceptions: Object relative pronoun can be omitted: the report (that) I sent. Subject pronoun normally cannot: the person who called.
Common mistakes:
❌ My manager, that lives nearby,... → ✅ My manager, who lives nearby,...
❌ The person called me. (если who = subject относительного clause) → ✅ The person who called me.
Don't confuse with: Defining = essential, no commas. Non-defining = extra, commas.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Defining → identifies.
Non-defining → extra information.
that only standard defining.
Object relative can sometimes be omitted.

Core idea: Participle clauses делают предложения короче и связывают связанные действия или описание.
Main rule / explanation: Present participle (-ing) can show simultaneous/related action. Past participle can give passive/background description. Perfect participle having + V3 shows earlier action.
Form / structure: -ing clause. V3 clause. Having + V3 clause.
When / why we use it: Используем participle clauses, чтобы сделать связанные действия или описания короче.
Examples:
Walking home, I saw an old friend. → Идя домой, я встретил старого друга.
The people working on the project are experienced. → Люди, работающие над проектом, опытны.
Built in 1920, the building is still in use. → Построенное в 1920 году здание всё ещё используется.
Having finished the report, she sent it to the client. → Закончив отчёт, она отправила его клиенту.
Special cases / exceptions: Subject of participle clause normally matches subject of main clause. Иначе возникает dangling participle.
Common mistakes:
❌ Walking down the street, the rain started. → Получается, будто дождь шёл по улице.
✅ Walking down the street, I got caught in the rain.
Don't confuse with: Проверь: кто выполняет action в participle clause? Это должен быть subject main clause.
Quick summary / memory hook:
-ing = related/current action.
V3 = passive/background description.
Having + V3 = earlier action.
Avoid dangling participle.

Lesson / Topic: Zero, first, second, and third conditionals
Core idea: Четыре major conditional patterns показывают разные отношения между reality и time.
Main rule / explanation: Zero = general truth. First = real future possibility. Second = unreal/unlikely present/future. Third = unreal past. Mixed forms connect different periods.
Form / structure: Zero: If + Present, Present. First: If + Present, will + V1. Second: If + Past, would + V1. Third: If + Past Perfect, would have + V3.
When / why we use it: Используем conditional pattern по сочетанию времени и reality.
Examples:
If you heat water to 100°C, it boils. → Если нагреть воду до 100°C, она кипит.
If it rains, we'll stay home. → Если пойдёт дождь, мы останемся дома.
If I had more time, I would travel more. → Если бы у меня было больше времени, я бы больше путешествовал.
If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train. → Если бы мы ушли раньше, мы бы успели на поезд.
Special cases / exceptions: Choice depends on reality and time, not on the word if itself. Mixed conditionals combine periods.
Common mistakes:
❌ «Есть if → всегда Second Conditional». → Нет.
❌ Every hypothetical sentence is Third. → Third is specifically unreal past.
Don't confuse with: Сначала определи: general, real future, unreal now/future или unreal past?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Zero → general truth.
First → realistic future.
Second → unreal now/future.
Third → unreal past.

Core idea: Некоторые verbs с двумя objects могут образовывать два типа passive sentence, и выбор зависит от того, какой объект хотим сделать focus.
Main rule / explanation: Active: They gave me the report / They gave the report to me. Passive: I was given the report / The report was given to me. With tell, personal object often becomes passive subject.
Form / structure: object-person + be + V3 + thing. thing + be + V3 + to + person.
When / why we use it: Используем passive, когда person или thing становится главным information focus.
Examples:
They gave me the report. → Они дали мне отчёт.
I was given the report. → Мне дали отчёт.
The report was given to me. → Отчёт был передан мне.
I was told about the change. → Мне сообщили об изменении.
Special cases / exceptions: Не каждый two-object verb допускает оба passive patterns equally naturally. Учи common constructions.
Common mistakes:
❌ Каждый verb with two objects автоматически имеет две одинаково естественные passive forms. → Нет.
✅ I was told about the change. — естественная модель с tell.
Don't confuse with: Спроси: что хочу сделать subject? person или thing?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Two-object active can have different passive focuses.
I was given the report.
The report was given to me.

Lesson / Topic: Possessive ’s with time expressions – Two hours’ walk
Core idea: Possessive forms with time expressions могут показывать duration или distance.
Main rule / explanation: Singular time noun: a day's work, one week's notice. Plural time noun ending in s: two weeks' holiday, five years' experience. Expressions can answer «how long?» and describe a distance/time needed.
Form / structure: singular time + 's. plural time ending in s + '.
When / why we use it: Используем, когда time expression функционирует как possessive modifier.
Examples:
a day's work. → работа на день.
three weeks' holiday. → трёхнедельный отпуск.
ten minutes' drive. → десять минут езды.
It's two hours' walk. → Это два часа пешком.
It's a two-hour walk. → Это двухчасовая прогулка.
Special cases / exceptions: Regular plural ending in s takes apostrophe only: hours', weeks', years'. Do not write hours's.
Common mistakes:
❌ two hours's walk → ✅ two hours' walk.
❌ five years's experience → ✅ five years' experience.
Don't confuse with: Compare possessive form and compound adjective: two hours' walk vs a two-hour walk.
Quick summary / memory hook:
singular time → 's.
regular plural time → s'.
No double s'.

Core idea: Compound adjectives объединяют два или более слова, которые вместе описывают noun.
Main rule / explanation: Частые patterns: well-known, full-time, user-friendly, high-speed, ten-year-old. Перед noun обычно используется hyphen.
Form / structure: word-word + noun. number + singular noun + adjective ending.
When / why we use it: Используем compound adjective как одно определение перед noun; часто нужен hyphen.
Examples:
a well-known company. → известная компания.
a full-time job. → работа на полный день.
a user-friendly interface. → удобный для пользователя интерфейс.
a five-year-old child. → пятилетний ребёнок.
a high-quality product. → высококачественный продукт.
Special cases / exceptions: В number-based compound noun remains singular: five-year-old, not five-years-old. После noun: The child is five years old.
Common mistakes:
❌ a ten-years project → ✅ a ten-year project.
❌ The child is five-year-old. → ✅ The child is five years old.
Don't confuse with: Перед noun compound acts as one adjective. After noun можно использовать обычное plural time expression.
Quick summary / memory hook:
compound adjective before noun → often hyphenated.
number + singular noun.
After noun → normal plural form.

Core idea: Многие nouns имеют устойчивые сочетания с определёнными prepositions. В professional English это важные collocations.
Main rule / explanation: Examples: access to, reason for, solution to, increase in, demand for, effect on, experience in, relationship with, interest in, responsibility for.
Form / structure: noun + preposition + noun/pronoun/V-ing where appropriate.
When / why we use it: Учи noun вместе с его typical preposition, а не пытайся переводить preposition отдельно.
Examples:
access to information. → доступ к информации.
reason for the delay. → причина задержки.
solution to the problem. → решение проблемы.
increase in prices. → рост цен.
demand for services. → спрос на услуги.
effect on performance. → влияние на performance.
experience in marketing. → опыт в маркетинге.
responsibility for the project. → ответственность за проект.
Special cases / exceptions: Preposition often not predictable from another language. В source emphasis is on memorizing the complete phrase.
Common mistakes: ❌ solution for the problem → ✅ solution to the problem.
Don't confuse with: Не учи «access» отдельно — учи «access to».
Quick summary / memory hook:
access to.
reason for.
solution to.
increase in.
demand for.
effect on.
experience in.
responsibility for.

Core idea: Comparatives можно усиливать или смягчать, а также использовать для описания постепенного изменения.
Main rule / explanation: A little/a bit/slightly show small difference. Much/far/a lot show large difference. Even adds emphasis. Comparative + and + comparative shows continuing change. The + comparative, the + comparative shows connected change.
Form / structure: slightly + comparative. much/far/a lot + comparative. even + comparative. comparative and comparative. the + comparative, the + comparative.
When / why we use it: Используем, когда важно не только сравнить, но и показать размер difference или process of change.
Examples:
slightly cheaper → немного дешевле.
a little faster → немного быстрее.
much more expensive → намного дороже.
far better → гораздо лучше.
a lot easier → намного легче.
even more useful → ещё полезнее.
The situation is getting better and better. → Ситуация становится всё лучше и лучше.
The more you practise, the easier it becomes. → Чем больше практикуешься, тем легче становится.
Special cases / exceptions: Standard comparative does not combine with very: very better is wrong. Use much better/far better.
Common mistakes:
❌ very better → ✅ much better.
❌ very more expensive → ✅ much more expensive.
Don't confuse with: Сначала basic comparative, затем modifier, если нужен размер difference.
Quick summary / memory hook:
a bit/slightly = small difference.
much/far/a lot = large difference.
even = extra emphasis.
- er and -er = continuing change.

Lesson / Topic: Reduced infinitives: Omitting the infinitive phrase after 'to'
Core idea: Reduced infinitives позволяют не повторять уже понятную часть infinitive phrase.
Main rule / explanation: После некоторых structures можно оставить только to. После modal может остаться bare verb omission с контекстом: I can help if you want me to. She should have.
Form / structure: want to / promise to etc. → to may remain. modal + understood verb can be omitted.
When / why we use it: Используем, когда listener легко восстанавливает пропущенные words из контекста.
Examples:
I want to go, but I can't. → Я хочу пойти, но не могу.
She didn't call, although she promised to. → Она не позвонила, хотя обещала.
I'd like to. → Я бы хотел.
He asked me to. → Он попросил меня.
I can help if you want me to. → Я могу помочь, если хочешь, чтобы я помог.
She didn't finish, although she should have. → Она не закончила, хотя должна была.
Special cases / exceptions: Ellipsis/reduced infinitive работает только при ясном context. Если omission создаёт ambiguity, words лучше повторить.
Common mistakes:
❌ Remove words so listener cannot reconstruct the action. → Тогда сокращение не подходит.
✅ She wants to go, and I want to. → Natural when go is understood.
Don't confuse with: Проверь: может ли listener восстановить missing verb phrase без догадки?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Reduced infinitive = avoid repetition.
After some expressions only to remains.
Modal can leave understood action.
Context is essential.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced present simple and present continuous
Core idea: Выбор Present Simple и Present Continuous здесь зависит не только от времени, но и от того, говорим ли мы о постоянной ситуации, временном действии, изменении или необычном повторении.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple чаще показывает устойчивую ситуацию, привычку, факт или состояние. Present Continuous показывает временную ситуацию, изменение или необычный/раздражающий повтор.
Form / structure: S + V1/V-s. S + am/is/are + V-ing.
When / why we use it: She works for an international company. = stable fact. She is working from home this month. = temporary. You're always interrupting me. = repeated behaviour viewed as irritating/temporary.
Examples:
She works for an international company. → Она работает в международной компании.
She is working from home this month. → В этом месяце она работает из дома.
More companies are moving their services online. → Всё больше компаний переводят свои услуги онлайн.
You're always interrupting me. → Ты всё время меня перебиваешь.
Special cases / exceptions: Некоторые traditionally stative verbs остаются non-continuous при state meaning: understand, believe, own. Но отдельные verbs меняют meaning и тогда могут стать continuous: I'm having lunch; I'm thinking about the proposal; We are seeing more customers this year.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am understanding the problem. → ✅ I understand the problem.
❌ She owns the company, so she is owning it. → ✅ She owns the company.
Don't confuse with: Не выбирай Continuous только потому, что действие происходит «сейчас». Смотри на meaning: state, activity, temporary situation или developing trend.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Simple → stable/state/repeated.
Continuous → temporary/developing/unusual behaviour.
Meaning matters more than «now».

Lesson / Topic: Advanced past simple, past continuous & past perfect
Core idea: Продвинутая работа с прошедшим временем — это организация narrative: что является основной последовательностью, что было фоном, что произошло раньше и что длилось до прошлого момента.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple = main completed events. Past Continuous = background/in-progress. Past Perfect = earlier past event. Past Perfect Continuous = duration/activity before a past point.
Form / structure: V2. was/were + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: She opened the file, checked the figures and sent the report. / She was checking the figures when the system crashed. / When we arrived, the meeting had already started. / She had been working for hours before she found the cause.
Examples:
She opened the file, checked the figures and sent the report. → Она открыла файл, проверила цифры и отправила отчёт.
She was checking the figures when the system crashed. → Она проверяла цифры, когда система упала.
When we arrived, the meeting had already started. → Когда мы пришли, встреча уже началась.
She had been working on the problem for hours before she found the cause. → Она работала над проблемой несколько часов, прежде чем нашла причину.
Special cases / exceptions: Past Perfect не нужен автоматически для каждого earlier action. Он полезен, когда relationship between past events важен с выбранной narrative viewpoint.
Common mistakes:
❌ Использовать Past Perfect в каждом предложении о прошлом. → Нужно показать конкретную связь с другой past point.
❌ She had been work... → ✅ She had been working...
Don't confuse with: Сначала построи timeline. Past Simple = main line; Past Continuous = background; Past Perfect = earlier; Past Perfect Continuous = duration before past point.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Simple = main events.
Past Continuous = background.
Past Perfect = earlier.
Past Perfect Continuous = duration before past point.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced modal verbs: will, would and should
Core idea: Will, would и should могут выражать не только будущее или совет. Их смысл зависит от ситуации.
Main rule / explanation: Will может показывать готовность, типичное поведение или уверенное предположение. Would может показывать привычку в прошлом или делать просьбу мягче. Should может показывать ожидание или то, что считается нормальным/ожидаемым.
Form / structure: will + V1. would + V1. should + V1. Formal conditional: Should + subject + V1...
When / why we use it: I'll help you. → willing. He will often ignore messages. → characteristic behaviour. That will be John calling. → strong expectation. Would you mind checking this? → polite request. The results should be ready by now. → expectation.
Examples:
I'll help you. → Я помогу тебе.
He will often ignore messages when he's busy. → Он часто игнорирует сообщения, когда занят.
That will be John calling. → Это, должно быть, Джон звонит.
Would you mind checking this? → Не могли бы вы это проверить?
The results should be ready by now. → Результаты, по идее, уже должны быть готовы.
Should you need assistance, contact the support team. → Если вам понадобится помощь, обратитесь в поддержку.
Special cases / exceptions: Значение modal зависит от context. Will be at home может быть prediction/strong expectation; would be at home — context-dependent, hypothetical или viewed from past; should be at home — expectation based on what is normally true.
Common mistakes:
❌ Учить will = только «буду». → На C1 значение зависит от context.
❌ Should always = совет. → It can also mean expectation or formal conditional.
Don't confuse with: Спроси: speaker is predicting, willing, describing a habit, softening, expecting or giving a formal condition?
Quick summary / memory hook:
will → willingness / typical behaviour / strong expectation.
would → past habit / softer request/opinion.
should → expectation / appropriateness / formal conditional.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced modal verbs: can / be able to, may / might
Core idea: Can и be able to оба выражают ability, но be able to становится важным в других tenses/aspects и для конкретного успешного события в прошлом. May/might выражают possibility.
Main rule / explanation: Can = ability now. Be able to удобен в future/perfect forms. Could = general past ability. Was/were able to или managed to часто яснее для one specific successful past event. May/might = possibility.
Form / structure: can + V1. be able to + V1. could + V1. may/might + V1. may/might have + V3.
When / why we use it: I can solve the problem. / We'll be able to access the system tomorrow. / We were able to solve the problem. / It may be true. / She might have forgotten.
Examples:
I can solve the problem. → Я могу решить проблему.
We'll be able to access the system tomorrow. → Завтра мы сможем получить доступ к системе.
We were able to solve the problem. → Нам удалось решить проблему.
It may be true. → Возможно, это правда.
She might have forgotten. → Возможно, она забыла.
Special cases / exceptions: Might иногда предполагает slightly lower certainty than may, но разница не всегда строгая. Could не всегда лучший вариант для one-off successful past event.
Common mistakes:
❌ I'll can access it tomorrow. → ✅ I'll be able to access it tomorrow.
❌ We could solve the specific problem yesterday. → Often clearer: We were able to solve the problem.
Don't confuse with: Can/could — modal. Be able to — flexible tense/aspect. May/might — possibility.
Quick summary / memory hook:
can → ability now.
be able to → flexible tense/aspect.
could → general past ability.
was able to/managed to → specific past success.
may/might → possibility.

Lesson / Topic: The subjunctive in English: Present and past
Core idea: English uses subjunctive-like forms mainly in formal recommendations, demands, necessity and hypothetical structures.
Main rule / explanation: Present subjunctive uses the base form after expressions such as essential, important, insist, demand: It is essential that she be present. British English often also uses should + infinitive. Past subjunctive is most visible in were.
Form / structure: that + subject + V1. Formal BrE: that + subject + should + V1. Hypothetical were: If I were..., I wish it were...
When / why we use it: It is essential that every applicant be informed. / They insisted that he leave immediately. / If I were you, I would wait.
Examples:
It is essential that every applicant be informed. → Очень важно, чтобы каждого кандидата проинформировали.
It is important that she be present. → Важно, чтобы она присутствовала.
They insisted that he leave immediately. → Они настояли, чтобы он немедленно ушёл.
If I were you, I would wait. → На твоём месте я бы подождал.
I wish it were easier. → Жаль, что это не проще.
Special cases / exceptions: В British English should + infinitive is also common after such expressions. Were in hypothetical structures marks unreality, not ordinary past time.
Common mistakes:
❌ It is essential that she is present. → In the formal subjunctive pattern: ✅ It is essential that she be present.
❌ If I was you... → Standard formal/hypothetical: ✅ If I were you...
Don't confuse with: Subjunctive form is selected by structure and meaning, not by ordinary tense sequence.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Formal recommendation/demand → base verb.
Hypothetical → were.
Past-looking form may mark unreality, not past time.

Lesson / Topic: The perfect tenses: Forms and uses
Core idea: Perfect forms показывают relationship между двумя reference points. Perfect не означает просто «прошедшее».
Main rule / explanation: Present Perfect links past to now. Present Perfect Continuous emphasizes duration/activity to now. Past Perfect places an event before a past reference point. Past Perfect Continuous emphasizes duration before a past point. Future Perfect and Future Perfect Continuous relate completion/duration to a future reference point.
Form / structure: have/has + V3. have/has been + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing. will have + V3. will have been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Главный вопрос: относительно какого reference point произошло действие и важен ли result, activity, duration или completion?
Examples:
I have finished the report. → Я закончил отчёт.
I have been working all morning. → Я работаю всё утро.
The meeting had started before we arrived. → Встреча началась до нашего прихода.
She had been waiting for an hour when he called. → Она ждала час, когда он позвонил.
By Friday, we will have completed the project. → К пятнице мы завершим проект.
By June, I will have been working here for ten years. → К июню я буду работать здесь уже десять лет.
Special cases / exceptions: Perfect is a relationship marker. Не выбирай форму только потому, что действие «в прошлом».
Common mistakes:
❌ Переводить Perfect как отдельное слово «уже». → Нужно смотреть на relationship between reference points.
❌ I had finished when I arrived. → Это меняет timeline: action was completed before arrival.
Don't confuse with: Сначала выбери reference point. Потом decide: completion/result or activity/duration.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Perfect = relationship between time points.
Simple Perfect → completion/result/experience.
Perfect Continuous → activity/duration.

Core idea: Participle clauses позволяют сжать несколько связанных идей в более короткую formal structure.
Main rule / explanation: Present participle, past participle, perfect participle и perfect passive могут выражать time, reason, result, condition или accompanying circumstances.
Form / structure: -ing clause. V3 clause. Having + V3. Having been + V3.
When / why we use it: Knowing the risks, they changed the plan. / Designed for small businesses, the system is easy to use. / Having completed the analysis, she presented the results. / Having been informed of the changes, the team adjusted the schedule.
Examples:
Knowing the risks, they changed the plan. → Зная риски, они изменили план.
Designed for small businesses, the system is easy to use. → Система, разработанная для малого бизнеса, проста в использовании.
Having completed the analysis, she presented the results. → Закончив анализ, она представила результаты.
Having been informed of the changes, the team adjusted the schedule. → Получив информацию об изменениях, команда скорректировала график.
Special cases / exceptions: Implied subject of participle clause normally matches main clause subject.
Common mistakes:
❌ Having finished the report, the meeting started. → Получается, будто meeting finished the report.
✅ Having finished the report, I went to the meeting.
Don't confuse with: Проверь: кто выполняет действие в participle clause? Этот же subject должен быть в main clause.
Quick summary / memory hook:
-ing = simultaneous/related action.
V3 = passive/background.
Having + V3 = earlier action.
Having been + V3 = earlier passive.

Core idea: Порядок слов можно менять, чтобы выделить важную часть сообщения, противопоставить идеи или поставить длинную информацию в более удобное место.
Main rule / explanation: Для выделения информации используются специальные конструкции: иногда часть предложения выносят вперёд, после отрицательных слов меняют порядок слов, а cleft-конструкции прямо показывают, что именно важно.
Form / structure: Normal order. Fronted phrase + clause. Negative adverbial + auxiliary + subject. It-cleft / What-cleft.
When / why we use it: This problem, we need to solve first. / Never have I seen such a result. / Only after the meeting did we understand the problem. / What we need is more time. / It was the deadline that caused the problem.
Examples:
This problem, we need to solve first. → Эту проблему нам нужно решить первой.
Never have I seen such a result. → Я никогда не видел такого результата.
Only after the meeting did we understand the problem. → Только после встречи мы поняли проблему.
What we need is more time. → То, что нам нужно, — это больше времени.
It was the deadline that caused the problem. → Именно deadline вызвал проблему.
Special cases / exceptions: Emphasis often requires a specific syntactic pattern. Simple word movement can produce an ungrammatical sentence.
Common mistakes:
❌ Never I have seen... → ✅ Never have I seen...
❌ Only after the meeting we understood... → ✅ Only after the meeting did we understand...
Don't confuse with: Сначала determine what information should be prominent, then choose the structure that creates that focus.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Fronting = emphasis.
Negative/restrictive fronting → inversion.
Cleft = explicit focus.
End-weight = long information later.

Core idea: Prepositions at C1 работают как часть larger patterns. Их нельзя надёжно выводить прямым переводом.
Main rule / explanation: Prepositions can follow verbs, adjectives and nouns. In questions/relative clauses they can stay at the end or move before whom/which in formal style. Preposition to is followed by -ing.
Form / structure: verb + prep. adjective + prep. noun + prep. preposition + V-ing. Wh + clause + prep.
When / why we use it: depend on, belong to, insist on, object to; responsible for, aware of, capable of, interested in; reason for, solution to, effect on, access to.
Examples:
I depend on the result. → Я завишу от результата.
She is responsible for the project. → Она отвечает за проект.
We need a solution to the problem. → Нам нужно решение проблемы.
Who did you speak to? → С кем ты говорил?
To whom did you speak? → С кем вы разговаривали? (formal)
I'm interested in learning. → Я заинтересован в изучении.
I look forward to hearing from you. → Жду вашего ответа.
Special cases / exceptions: To can be a preposition, not infinitive marker: look forward to hearing, object to paying.
Common mistakes:
❌ I look forward to hear from you. → ✅ I look forward to hearing from you.
❌ access of the system → ✅ access to the system.
Don't confuse with: Учи noun/verb/adjective together with its preposition.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Verb + prep.
Adjective + prep.
Noun + prep.
Preposition to + V-ing.
Formal preposition placement → whom/which.

Core idea: Subject–verb agreement становится сложнее, когда subject separated from verb, содержит quantifiers или является collective noun/amount expression.
Main rule / explanation: Verb agrees with grammatical subject, not the nearest noun. Each/every/everyone take singular verb. Collective nouns can vary by variety and meaning. Amounts/periods can take singular when seen as one unit. Titles usually singular.
Form / structure: singular subject + singular verb. plural subject + plural verb.
When / why we use it: The list of required documents is on the website. / Each employee is responsible. / Everyone has received the message. / Ten minutes is enough. / Five years is a long time.
Examples:
The list of required documents is on the website. → Список необходимых документов находится на сайте.
Each employee is responsible for the result. → Каждый сотрудник отвечает за результат.
Everyone has received the message. → Все получили сообщение.
Ten minutes is enough. → Десяти минут достаточно.
“Great Expectations” is a novel. → «Большие надежды» — роман.
Special cases / exceptions: Collective nouns can vary: The team is working... / In some British contexts, the team are discussing... Meaning and variety matter.
Common mistakes:
❌ The list of changes are ready. → ✅ The list of changes is ready.
❌ The nearest noun controls the verb. → ✅ Согласование определяется настоящим подлежащим.
Don't confuse with: Не смотри на nearest noun. Найди real grammatical subject.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Subject controls agreement.
Don't be distracted by intervening nouns.
each/every/everyone → singular.
Amounts/titles can be singular as units.

Core idea: Above и over оба могут означать положение выше, но over чаще связан с покрытием, пересечением или движением через что-то.
Main rule / explanation: Above = at a higher level/position. Over = covering/extending across, movement across; over часто используется и с numbers/quantities.
Form / structure: above + noun. over + noun.
When / why we use it: Выбирай по смыслу: просто выше → above; покрывает/пересекает/движется через → over.
Examples:
The picture is above the sofa. → Картина над диваном.
The temperature is above zero. → Температура выше нуля.
There is a bridge over the river. → Над рекой есть мост.
We flew over the mountains. → Мы летели над горами.
Over 500 people attended. → Пришло более 500 человек.
Special cases / exceptions: В некоторых contexts оба варианта возможны. Важен основной relation.
Common mistakes: ❌ Использовать above автоматически для любого «над». → Если важен crossing/covering, over часто естественнее.
Don't confuse with:
above = higher level.
over = covering/crossing/movement; часто > numbers.
Quick summary / memory hook:
above → higher.
over → across/covering/movement.

Core idea: Although и however оба выражают contrast, но грамматически это разные инструменты.
Main rule / explanation: Although introduces subordinate clause. However is a linking adverb connecting ideas and usually needs punctuation.
Form / structure: although + clause. Sentence. However, sentence.
When / why we use it: Хотим одну dependent clause → although. Хотим связать две самостоятельные идеи → however.
Examples:
Although it was expensive, we bought it. → Хотя это было дорого, мы купили это.
It was expensive. However, we bought it. → Это было дорого. Однако мы купили это.
The solution is, however, quite expensive. → Решение, однако, довольно дорогое.
Special cases / exceptions: В standard concise usage не ставь however прямо после although.
Common mistakes:
❌ Although it was expensive, however, we bought it. → ✅ Although it was expensive, we bought it.
❌ However it was expensive, we bought it. → ✅ Although it was expensive, we bought it.
Don't confuse with: although = grammar connector inside one structure. however = linking adverb.
Quick summary / memory hook:
although + clause.
however + separate idea/punctuation.

Lesson / Topic: Amount of vs Number of vs Quantity of
Core idea: Number of, amount of и quantity of выбираются по типу noun и смыслу количества.
Main rule / explanation: Number of → plural countable nouns. Amount of → uncountable nouns. Quantity of → countable or uncountable, especially measurable quantity.
Form / structure: the/a large number of + plural noun. the/a large amount of + uncountable. the/a large quantity of + countable/uncountable.
When / why we use it: Countable employees/questions → number. Uncountable money/information/traffic → amount. Measurable quantity → quantity.
Examples:
The number of employees has increased. → Количество сотрудников увеличилось.
The amount of traffic has increased. → Объём трафика увеличился.
A large quantity of water was needed. → Потребовалось большое количество воды.
Special cases / exceptions: Quantity of can occur with both countable and uncountable; it focuses on measurable quantity.
Common mistakes:
❌ the amount of employees → ✅ the number of employees.
❌ a number of money → ✅ an amount of money.
Don't confuse with: Сначала countable or uncountable?
Quick summary / memory hook:
number → plural countable.
amount → uncountable.
quantity → both, measurable.

Lesson / Topic: How to avoid double subjects in English
Core idea: В стандартном английском clause обычно имеет один grammatical subject. Не добавляй pronoun после noun, который уже является subject.
Main rule / explanation: Normal: The manager approved the request. Нейтрально не нужно: The manager, he approved... В relative clause тоже нельзя добавлять лишний subject.
Form / structure: one grammatical subject per clause. Relative clause keeps its own subject/object structure.
When / why we use it: Сначала найди subject и проверь, не повторяешь ли его вторым pronoun.
Examples:
The manager approved the request. → Менеджер утвердил запрос.
The report that I sent yesterday is ready. → Отчёт, который я вчера отправил, готов.
Here, that is the object of sent, not an extra subject.
Special cases / exceptions: В разговорной речи possible marked pattern My brother, he works in IT., но это не neutral standard structure.
Common mistakes:
❌ The manager, he approved the request. → ✅ The manager approved the request.
❌ The report that I sent it yesterday... → ✅ The report that I sent yesterday...
Don't confuse with: Не добавляй pronoun, если noun уже выполняет роль subject/object в структуре.
Quick summary / memory hook:
One clause → one normal subject.
Avoid repeated subject pronouns.

Core idea: Between и among связаны с положением/отношениями внутри группы, но важен не только count предметов.
Main rule / explanation: Between традиционно связано с two, но может использоваться с more than two, когда рассматриваются individual relationships. Among = внутри группы/распределение.
Form / structure: between + people/things. among + group.
When / why we use it: Use between when individual items/relationships are in focus. Among when inside a group or distributed within it.
Examples:
The agreement is between the two companies. → Соглашение между двумя компаниями.
The negotiations between the five countries continued. → Переговоры между пятью странами продолжились.
She was sitting among her colleagues. → Она сидела среди коллег.
The money was divided among the participants. → Деньги разделили между участниками/среди участников.
Special cases / exceptions: Не учи простое правило «between = 2, among = 3+» как абсолютное.
Common mistakes: ❌ Between can only be used with two. → Нет: between five countries possible when individual relationships are considered.
Don't confuse with: Смотри, individual relationships или group context?
Quick summary / memory hook:
between → individual relationships/items.
among → within a group/distribution.

Core idea: Bring и take выбираются по viewpoint: движение к speaker/reference point или от него.
Main rule / explanation: Bring = movement toward the speaker or place being discussed. Take = movement away from speaker/current location.
Form / structure: bring + object + to destination. take + object + to destination.
When / why we use it: Представь точку зрения говорящего: куда движется object относительно этой reference point?
Examples:
Bring your laptop to the meeting. → Принеси ноутбук на встречу.
Take these documents to the manager. → Отнеси эти документы менеджеру.
Can you bring the report to my office? → Можешь принести отчёт в мой офис?
Can you take this report to Sarah? → Можешь отнести этот отчёт Саре?
Special cases / exceptions: Главное — viewpoint, не просто физическое направление предмета.
Common mistakes: ❌ Выбирать bring/take только по движению предмета. → Смотри, где speaker/reference point.
Don't confuse with:
bring → toward reference point.
take → away from reference point.
Quick summary / memory hook: Viewpoint decides bring vs take.

Core idea: Clean и wash оба могут относиться к удалению грязи, но focus разный.
Main rule / explanation: Clean = сделать чистым, убрать грязь/пыль/нежелательный материал. Wash = использовать water/liquid в процессе cleaning.
Form / structure: clean + object. wash + object.
When / why we use it: Когда важен общий результат «очистить» → clean. Когда важен water/liquid → wash.
Examples:
Clean the kitchen. → Убери/очисти кухню.
I cleaned my shoes. → Я почистил обувь.
Wash your hands. → Вымой руки.
I washed the car. → Я помыл машину.
The equipment must be cleaned regularly. → Оборудование нужно регулярно очищать.
Special cases / exceptions: Некоторые objects можно both clean and wash: clean the windows = remove dirt; wash the windows = use water.
Common mistakes:
❌ Wash the kitchen. (если общий процесс уборки) → ✅ Clean the kitchen.
❌ Clean your hands. → In normal everyday usage: Wash your hands.
Don't confuse with: clean = remove dirt / make clean. wash = clean using water/liquid.
Quick summary / memory hook:
clean = general cleaning.
wash = with water/liquid.

Core idea: Come и go зависят от reference point: движение к speaker/listener/shared destination или от reference point.
Main rule / explanation: Come = movement toward speaker or another shared reference point. Go = movement away from that point.
Form / structure: come + destination. go + destination.
When / why we use it: Смотри на viewpoint speaker/listener/shared destination.
Examples:
Come here. → Иди сюда.
Are you coming to the meeting? → Ты придёшь на встречу?
I'm going home. → Я иду/еду домой.
She went to the office. → Она пошла в офис.
Special cases / exceptions: Reference point может быть shared destination, даже если speaker ещё там не находится.
Common mistakes: ❌ Выбирать come/go только по тому, находится ли speaker уже на месте. → Shared destination can be reference point.
Don't confuse with:
come → toward reference point.
go → away from reference point.
Quick summary / memory hook: Reference point decides come vs go.

Core idea: Have been to и have gone to различаются тем, вернулся ли человек из места к reference time.
Main rule / explanation: Have been to = visited and returned. Have gone to = went there and is still away / not returned at reference time.
Form / structure: have/has been to + place. have/has gone to + place.
When / why we use it: Для life experience → been to. Для current absence/presence elsewhere → gone to.
Examples:
I've been to London twice. → Я дважды был в Лондоне.
Sarah has gone to the supermarket. → Сара ушла в супермаркет.
Tom has been to Spain. → Том был в Испании.
Tom has gone to Spain. → Том уехал в Испанию и ещё не вернулся.
Special cases / exceptions: Context decides whether person has returned.
Common mistakes: ❌ I've gone to London twice. (если речь о past experience and return) → ✅ I've been to London twice.
Don't confuse with:
been to = visited and returned.
gone to = went and is still away.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Experience → been.
Currently away → gone.

Core idea: If и whether оба могут вводить indirect yes/no question, но whether имеет дополнительные grammatical uses.
Main rule / explanation: If/whether both possible in many indirect questions. Whether is preferred/more formal in some contexts and required before infinitive, with or not, and after a preposition.
Form / structure: if/whether + clause. whether + to + V1. whether or not + clause. prep + whether + clause.
When / why we use it: Смотри на position: simple indirect question часто допускает both; special constructions → whether.
Examples:
I don't know if she is coming. → Я не знаю, придёт ли она.
I don't know whether she is coming. → Я не знаю, придёт ли она.
We need to decide whether to stay. → Нам нужно решить, оставаться ли.
I don't know whether or not he agrees. → Я не знаю, согласен ли он или нет.
It depends on whether they accept. → Это зависит от того, примут ли они.
Special cases / exceptions: Whether особенно удобно ставить перед to + V1, после предлога и в конструкции whether or not.
Common mistakes:
❌ decide if to stay → ✅ decide whether to stay.
❌ It depends on if they accept. → ✅ It depends on whether they accept.
Don't confuse with: В обычном indirect yes/no question both may work. In special positions → whether.
Quick summary / memory hook:
if/whether = indirect yes/no question.
whether + to V1.
whether or not.
preposition + whether.

Core idea: Instead и instead of оба показывают alternative, но грамматически работают по-разному.
Main rule / explanation: Instead = adverb. Instead of = preposition and is followed by noun, pronoun or V-ing.
Form / structure: instead. instead of + noun/pronoun/V-ing.
When / why we use it: Instead часто заменяет whole alternative: We didn't take the train. We drove instead. Instead of вводит заменяемое действие/object.
Examples:
We didn't take the train. We drove instead. → Мы не поехали поездом. Вместо этого мы поехали на машине.
Instead, we decided to walk. → Вместо этого мы решили пойти пешком.
We walked instead of taking the bus. → Мы пошли пешком вместо автобуса.
She called instead of sending an email. → Она позвонила вместо того, чтобы отправлять email.
Special cases / exceptions: После instead of, если дальше verb, используем -ing.
Common mistakes:
❌ instead of wait → ✅ instead of waiting.
❌ We drove instead of the train. → Better meaning depends on intended structure: We drove instead.
Don't confuse with: adverb vs preposition.
Quick summary / memory hook:
instead = as an alternative.
instead of + noun/pronoun/V-ing.

Core idea: Its и it's отличаются так же чётко, как possessive и contraction.
Main rule / explanation: Its = possessive determiner. It's = it is or it has.
Form / structure: its + noun. it's = it is / it has.
When / why we use it: Проверь, можно ли заменить it's на it is или it has.
Examples:
The company changed its policy. → Компания изменила свою политику.
It's cold today. → Сегодня холодно.
It's been a long day. → День был долгим.
Special cases / exceptions: Possessive its does not take apostrophe.
Common mistakes:
❌ The company changed it's policy. → ✅ The company changed its policy.
❌ Its cold today. → ✅ It's cold today.
Don't confuse with: Possession → its. Contraction → it's.
Quick summary / memory hook:
its = possessive.
it's = it is / it has.

Lesson / Topic: Last vs The last, Next vs The next
Core idea: Last и next меняют смысл в зависимости от наличия the. Без the они часто относятся к периоду относительно now; с the — к конкретному элементу в sequence.
Main rule / explanation: Last week = week immediately before this one. The last week of the course = final week of that course. Next week = following week from now. The next week = following week in a sequence/narrative.
Form / structure: last/next + time period. the last/the next + noun in a sequence.
When / why we use it: Смотри, говорим ли мы о calendar period relative to now или about an item in a specific sequence.
Examples:
I saw her last week. → Я видел её на прошлой неделе.
The last week of the course was difficult. → Последняя неделя курса была сложной.
I'll see you next week. → Увидимся на следующей неделе.
The next week was much quieter. → Следующая неделя была намного спокойнее.
Special cases / exceptions: Article changes the meaning depending on context.
Common mistakes: ❌ Treat next month and the next month as always identical. → Context distinguishes them.
Don't confuse with:
last/next = relation to now often.
the last/the next = item in a sequence/context.
Quick summary / memory hook: Article changes the reference point.

Core idea: Lie и lay отличаются тем, является ли глагол intransitive «лежать» или transitive «класть что-то».
Main rule / explanation: Lie = be in a horizontal position: lie–lay–lain. Lay = put something somewhere: lay–laid–laid.
Form / structure: lie + no direct object. lay + direct object.
When / why we use it: Смотри, есть ли object: I lie down. / I lay the book down.
Examples:
I need to lie down. → Мне нужно лечь.
She is lying on the bed. → Она лежит на кровати.
Please lay the book on the table. → Положи книгу на стол.
He laid the keys on the desk. → Он положил ключи на стол.
Special cases / exceptions: Past of lie (recline) is lay. Lay has its own past laid. Именно это часто вызывает confusion.
Common mistakes:
❌ Yesterday I laid on the sofa. → ✅ Yesterday I lay on the sofa.
❌ He lay the keys on the desk. → ✅ He laid the keys on the desk.
Don't confuse with: lie = position/state. lay = put something.
Quick summary / memory hook:
lie – lay – lain.
lay – laid – laid.
Object after lay.

Core idea: Fewer обычно используется с plural countable nouns, less — с uncountable nouns.
Main rule / explanation: fewer mistakes/employees/problems. less time/money/information. In measurement expressions less can be natural: less than ten minutes.
Form / structure: fewer + plural countable. less + uncountable.
When / why we use it: Сначала определи grammatical type noun.
Examples:
We need fewer meetings. → Нам нужно меньше совещаний.
We need less paperwork. → Нам нужно меньше бумажной работы.
It took less than ten minutes. → Это заняло меньше десяти минут.
Special cases / exceptions: В measurement expressions less common: less than five kilometres. Не выбирай только по тому, что в русском это «отдельные вещи».
Common mistakes:
❌ less employees → ✅ fewer employees.
❌ fewer information → ✅ less information.
Don't confuse with:
countable plural → fewer.
uncountable → less.
Quick summary / memory hook:
fewer = countable plural.
less = uncountable.

Core idea: Like и as могут переводиться похоже, но like обычно сравнивает, а as вводит clause или показывает role/function.
Main rule / explanation: Like is usually preposition before noun/pronoun. As can introduce a clause or describe a role/function.
Form / structure: like + noun/pronoun. as + clause. as + role/noun.
When / why we use it: Спроси: «похож на?» → like. «в роли/так, как» → as.
Examples:
She works like a professional. → Она работает как профессионал (похоже на профессионала).
It looks like rain. → Похоже на дождь.
Do it as I showed you. → Сделай так, как я тебе показал.
He works as a designer. → Он работает дизайнером.
As you know, the meeting starts at nine. → Как ты знаешь, встреча начинается в девять.
Special cases / exceptions: В более формальной речи as обычно используется перед полноценной частью предложения: Do it as I told you.
Common mistakes:
❌ He works like a designer. (если это actual role) → ✅ He works as a designer.
❌ Do it like I told you. → Standard formal: ✅ Do it as I told you.
Don't confuse with:
like = resemblance.
as = role/function or clause.
Quick summary / memory hook:
like + noun/pronoun.
as + clause/role.

Lesson / Topic: Little vs A little, Few vs A few
Core idea: Little/few без a часто передают значение «мало, почти недостаточно». A little/a few показывают небольшой, но реальный amount/number.
Main rule / explanation: Little + uncountable. A little + uncountable. Few + plural countable. A few + plural countable.
Form / structure: little/a little + uncountable. few/a few + plural countable.
When / why we use it: Главное отличие — article a меняет оттенок: almost none/insufficient vs some amount/number.
Examples:
We have little time. → У нас мало времени, вероятно, недостаточно.
We have a little time. → У нас есть немного времени.
Few people understood the problem. → Мало кто понял проблему.
A few people understood the problem. → Несколько человек поняли проблему.
Special cases / exceptions: Article a changes meaning significantly. Сравни little hope vs a little hope.
Common mistakes:
❌ a little people → ✅ a few people.
❌ a few time → ✅ a little time.
Don't confuse with:
little/a little → uncountable.
few/a few → plural countable.
a = small but real amount/number.
Quick summary / memory hook:
a little/a few = some.
little/few = not much/not many.

Core idea: See, look и watch описывают разные виды visual perception.
Main rule / explanation: See = perception without deliberate effort. Look = direct your eyes toward something and normally needs at + object. Watch = observe for a period, especially something moving/changing.
Form / structure: see + object. look at + object. watch + object.
When / why we use it: Спроси: просто заметить → see. Направить взгляд → look at. Наблюдать некоторое время → watch.
Examples:
I can see the mountains. → Я вижу горы.
Look at this picture. → Посмотри на эту картинку.
We watched a film. → Мы посмотрели фильм.
She watched the children playing. → Она наблюдала, как дети играют.
Special cases / exceptions: Look needs at in the basic pattern when you mean direct your eyes toward something.
Common mistakes:
❌ Look the screen. → ✅ Look at the screen.
❌ I watched the mountains from the window. → Usually: I saw the mountains / looked at the mountains, depending on intended meaning.
Don't confuse with:
see = perception.
look at = directed attention.
watch = sustained observation.
Quick summary / memory hook:
see = notice.
look at = direct eyes.
watch = observe over time.

Core idea: Maybe и may be звучат одинаково, но это разные грамматические конструкции.
Main rule / explanation: Maybe = adverb meaning perhaps. May be = modal may + verb be.
Form / structure: Maybe + clause. subject + may be + complement.
When / why we use it: Если можно заменить на perhaps → maybe. Если modal + be является частью verb phrase → may be.
Examples:
Maybe she is busy. → Возможно, она занята.
She may be busy. → Возможно, она занята.
Maybe we'll go tomorrow. → Может быть, мы поедем завтра.
They may be late. → Возможно, они опоздают.
Special cases / exceptions: Position reveals structure: Maybe often stands at sentence level; may be is part of predicate.
Common mistakes:
❌ She maybe busy. → ✅ She may be busy. / Maybe she is busy.
❌ Maybe she may be busy. → Possible but changes emphasis; don't use one as a spelling variant of the other.
Don't confuse with:
maybe = perhaps.
may be = modal + be.
Quick summary / memory hook:
maybe = one word adverb.
may be = two-word verb phrase.

Core idea: Never и ever оба связаны с time/frequency, но работают по-разному.
Main rule / explanation: Never = at no time. Ever is common in questions, conditionals and superlative-like expressions.
Form / structure: never + verb. Have you ever...? if you ever... best ... I've ever...
When / why we use it: Ever часто используется, когда спрашиваем «когда-нибудь?» или говорим «когда-либо». Never уже содержит negative meaning.
Examples:
I've never been there. → Я никогда там не был.
She never complains. → Она никогда не жалуется.
Have you ever been to Spain? → Ты когда-нибудь был в Испании?
If you ever need help, call me. → Если тебе когда-нибудь понадобится помощь, позвони мне.
This is the best result I've ever seen. → Это лучший результат, который я когда-либо видел.
Special cases / exceptions: В standalone affirmative statement ever обычно не заменяет never.
Common mistakes: ❌ I've ever seen it. → ✅ I've never seen it. / This is the best I've ever seen.
Don't confuse with:
never = no time.
ever = questions/conditions/experience/emphasis.
Quick summary / memory hook:
never = at no time.
ever = at any time, commonly in questions/conditions.

Lesson / Topic: On the other hand vs On the contrary
Core idea: On the other hand и on the contrary оба могут связывать идеи, но выражают разные отношения.
Main rule / explanation: On the other hand introduces another side/aspect of an issue. On the contrary directly contradicts or corrects a previous statement/assumption.
Form / structure: Sentence. On the other hand, sentence. / On the contrary, sentence.
When / why we use it: Используй on the other hand, когда показываешь другую сторону; on the contrary — когда говоришь «наоборот, это не так».
Examples:
The job is well paid. On the other hand, the hours are long. → Работа хорошо оплачивается. С другой стороны, часы длинные.
“I thought the task was difficult.” “On the contrary, it was quite easy.” → «Я думал, задание сложное». «Наоборот, оно довольно лёгкое».
Special cases / exceptions: On the contrary requires direct contradiction/correction, not merely different information.
Common mistakes:
❌ Two different facts = automatically on the contrary. → Нет; often on the other hand.
✅ On the contrary, it was easy. → direct correction.
Don't confuse with:
other hand = another aspect.
contrary = opposite of what was suggested.
Quick summary / memory hook:
on the other hand = другой аспект.
on the contrary = прямое опровержение.

Core idea: Raise и rise различаются transitivity: raise обычно требует object, rise — обычно нет.
Main rule / explanation: Raise = someone raises something. Rise = something rises by itself. Forms: raise–raised–raised; rise–rose–risen.
Form / structure: raise + object. rise + subject/no direct object.
When / why we use it: Спроси: кто-то поднимает/увеличивает что-то? → raise. Что-то само повышается/поднимается? → rise.
Examples:
They raised the price. → Они повысили цену.
She raised her hand. → Она подняла руку.
Prices rise. → Цены растут.
The sun rises. → Солнце встаёт.
The temperature is rising. → Температура повышается.
Special cases / exceptions: Rise is intransitive in this basic distinction. Raise takes a direct object.
Common mistakes:
❌ They rose the price. → ✅ They raised the price.
❌ She raised. → Needs object in this meaning: She raised her hand.
Don't confuse with:
raise = transitive.
rise = intransitive.
Quick summary / memory hook:
raise–raised–raised.
rise–rose–risen.
Object → raise.

Lesson / Topic: Remember & Forget: To Do vs Doing
Core idea: Remember/forget + to V1 относятся к действию, которое нужно/нужно было выполнить. + V-ing — к memory of an action that happened.
Main rule / explanation: to-infinitive = task/action to do. V-ing = memory/experience of doing.
Form / structure: remember/forget + to + V1. remember/forget + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Сравни: Did I remember the task? vs Do I remember the event?
Examples:
Remember to send the email. → Не забудь отправить письмо.
I forgot to call him. → Я забыл ему позвонить.
I remember meeting her. → Я помню, как с ней познакомился.
I'll never forget visiting that place. → Я никогда не забуду, что побывал в том месте.
I remembered to lock the door. → Я не забыл запереть дверь.
I remember locking the door. → Я помню, как запер дверь.
Special cases / exceptions: Разница не просто во времени. Она в relationship between remembering and the action.
Common mistakes:
❌ I forgot meeting her. = «я забыл, что должен был с ней встретиться». → ✅ I forgot to meet her. (забыл сделать).
❌ I remembered meeting her. = «я вспомнил, что должен был встретиться». → ✅ I remember meeting her. (помню произошедшую встречу).
Don't confuse with:
to do = remember/forget the task.
doing = memory of past action.
Quick summary / memory hook:
remember/forget + to do → task.
remember/forget + doing → memory.

Core idea: Say и tell оба передают информацию, но tell обычно требует object — человека, которому что-то сообщают.
Main rule / explanation: Say focuses on words/message. Tell focuses on communicating to someone and usually takes an object in this reporting pattern.
Form / structure:
say something / say that...
tell someone something / tell someone to do something
tell the truth / tell a story / tell a joke / tell the time
When / why we use it: Сначала определи, назван ли receiver of message.
Examples:
She said that she was tired. → Она сказала, что устала.
She told me that she was tired. → Она сказала мне, что устала.
He told us the truth. → Он сказал нам правду.
He told a joke. → Он рассказал шутку.
Tell me the time, please. → Скажи мне, который час.
Special cases / exceptions: После tell действительно часто называют получателя, но не всегда. Устойчивые сочетания tell the truth, tell a lie, tell a story, tell a joke, tell the time употребляются без него.
Common mistakes:
❌ He said me the truth. → ✅ He told me the truth.
❌ He told me to the truth. → ✅ He told me the truth.
❌ She told that she was tired. → ✅ She said that she was tired. / She told me that she was tired.
❌ He said a joke. → ✅ He told a joke.
Don't confuse with:
say = words/message.
tell = tell someone.
Quick summary / memory hook:
say something.
say that...
tell someone something.
tell someone to do.

Lesson / Topic: Try to do vs Try doing
Core idea: Try to do и try doing оба могут переводиться как «попробовать», но focus разный.
Main rule / explanation: Try to do = make an effort to perform an action. Try doing = experiment with an action/method to see whether it works.
Form / structure: try + to + V1. try + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Спроси: речь о попытке выполнить action или об эксперименте с возможным solution?
Examples:
Try to restart the computer. → Попробуй перезапустить компьютер.
I tried to contact the client. → Я попытался связаться с клиентом.
Try restarting the computer. → Попробуй перезапустить компьютер (как способ решения).
Try using a different browser. → Попробуй другой браузер.
Special cases / exceptions: Это не просто two stylistic alternatives. Infinitive focuses on effort; -ing often suggests method/experiment.
Common mistakes:
❌ Try to restarting the computer. → ✅ Try restarting the computer.
❌ Try doing to contact the client. → ✅ Try to contact the client.
Don't confuse with:
to do = effort.
doing = experiment/method.
Quick summary / memory hook:
try to do = make an effort.
try doing = test a method.

Core idea: Until и by отвечают на разные вопросы о времени: продолжалось до момента или должно завершиться не позже deadline.
Main rule / explanation: Until = situation/action continues up to a time. By = deadline/latest time something will happen.
Form / structure: verb + until + time. verb + by + time.
When / why we use it: Для continuous duration → until. Для deadline/completion → by.
Examples:
I'll work until six. → Я буду работать до шести.
She stayed there until Friday. → Она оставалась там до пятницы.
Please finish it by six. → Закончи это к шести.
I'll have sent the report by Friday. → Я отправлю отчёт к пятнице.
Special cases / exceptions: Until can mean «не раньше», depending on context: Send it until Friday is not a normal way to express a deadline.
Common mistakes:
❌ Please finish it until six. → ✅ Please finish it by six.
✅ I won't send it until Friday. → Здесь until means «не раньше пятницы».
Don't confuse with:
until = continuation up to a time.
by = deadline/latest time.
Quick summary / memory hook:
until → continues to.
by → completed no later than.

Core idea: Whereas и while оба могут сравнивать две ситуации, но while имеет дополнительные meanings.
Main rule / explanation: Whereas mainly contrasts facts/characteristics. While can contrast, express time, or sometimes concession.
Form / structure: whereas + clause. while + clause.
When / why we use it: Если нужен только contrast between facts → whereas. Если while — determine from context whether it means time or contrast.
Examples:
The first option is cheap, whereas the second is faster. → Первый вариант дешёвый, тогда как второй быстрее.
The first option is cheap, while the second is faster. → Первый вариант дешёвый, тогда как второй быстрее.
While I was working, she called. → Пока я работал, она позвонила.
While I understand your point, I disagree. → Хотя я понимаю твою точку зрения, я не согласен.
Special cases / exceptions: Whereas is more formal and especially common in writing. While can mean during the time that or contrast/concession.
Common mistakes:
❌ Assume every while = whereas. → Нет: while can be time.
✅ While I was working... = time, not contrast.
Don't confuse with:
whereas = contrast.
while = contrast OR time OR concession.
Quick summary / memory hook:
whereas → contrastive.
while → contrast/time/concession.

Core idea: Wish, hope и expect связаны с future/desired situations, но выражают разное отношение к reality.
Main rule / explanation: Hope = desired and realistically possible. Expect = believe something is likely/anticipated. Wish = unreal, unlikely or impossible situation, or regret.
Form / structure: hope + clause/to V1. expect + noun/to V1/that-clause. wish + unreal structure.
When / why we use it: Используем, чтобы различить realistic desire, expectation и unreal/regret.
Examples:
I hope we can finish today. → Я надеюсь, что мы сможем закончить сегодня.
I expect the meeting to finish at five. → Я ожидаю, что встреча закончится в пять.
I wish I had more time. → Жаль, что у меня нет больше времени.
I wish you were here. → Жаль, что тебя здесь нет.
We wish you a pleasant journey. → Желаем вам приятного путешествия.
Special cases / exceptions: Wish is not a simple synonym for hope when the desired event is realistically possible.
Common mistakes:
❌ I wish we can finish today. → For realistic possibility: ✅ I hope we can finish today.
❌ I expect I had more time. → For unreal present: ✅ I wish I had more time.
Don't confuse with: Спроси: realistic desire → hope; likely expectation → expect; unreal/regret → wish.
Quick summary / memory hook:
hope = desired + possible.
expect = likely/anticipated.
wish = unreal/regret.
